parts.text:
23 Diffraction is a term used to describe one aspect of wave behaviour.
What does diffraction make possible?
A
the ability to hear around corners
B
the ability to hear high frequency and low frequency sound waves
C
the ability to hear loud and quiet sounds
D
the ability to hear sound through a brick wall

hints: Notice the question asks what diffraction makes possible for sound near an obstacle like a corner.
Recall that diffraction is spreading of a wave when it meets an edge or gap of similar size to its wavelength.
Compare bending round an obstacle with hearing different pitches, different loudnesses, and transmission through a solid wall.
walkthrough: Identify the key idea: diffraction means a wave spreads out after passing an edge, doorway or corner instead of travelling only in straight lines.
For sound, wavelengths are about $0.02 \text{ m}$ to $20 \text{ m}$, which are similar in size to doors, walls and corners, so spreading is large.
This spreading lets sound energy reach the region behind the obstacle where there is no direct line of sight.
Hearing high or low frequency is about frequency, and hearing loud or quiet is about amplitude, neither of which is caused by diffraction.
Hearing through a brick wall needs transmission through the solid, not bending around it.
Therefore diffraction explains hearing sound from a source that is out of sight round a corner. This is option A.

A.explanation: Diffraction is the spreading of waves past an edge or through a gap, so sound can bend round a corner into the shadow region.

B.explanation: Hearing different frequencies depends on pitch response of the ear, not on spreading of waves round obstacles.

C.explanation: Hearing loud and quiet sounds depends on amplitude and intensity, not on diffraction.

D.explanation: Sound heard through a wall is transmitted through the material, not diffracted around an edge or gap.
